trigger: a multi-replica deployment dispatching Broadcast via the legacy /instructions/{plugin}/{action} REST forwarder, targeting an agent connected only to a different replica

trigger: concurrent local registry churn (register/deregister) landing between local_agent_count()'s lock and known_agent_ids()'s separate lock, coincidentally matching sizes while sets differ
summary: The original fast-path gate compared local_agent_count() and known_agent_ids().size() via two non-atomic lock acquisitions — a race could silently take the fast path while a presence-only id was genuinely in the candidate set, with no not_sent entry and no metric.
disposition_note: Fixed: replaced with AgentRegistry::has_remote_presence(candidates), a single-lock direct membership check against the already-fetched candidate list — closes the race by construction, not just narrows it. New regression test added (same-size-different-membership).

trigger: disconnect ordering: local removal is synchronous, presence-row removal is a separate Postgres call, and live_presence()'s cache can additionally lag up to 3s
summary: A genuinely-departed agent can surface via a stale/cached presence row for up to ~3s after local removal, widening the pre-cache window.
disposition_note: Accepted as within the documented eventual-consistency tolerance (over-inclusion is safe by design); up-1's fix removes the race component this fed. No standalone fix required; not a defect on reflection.

trigger: concurrent disconnect(A)+reconnect(B) under different sessions
summary: Verified CLOSED: remove_if_session's session-guarded RETURNING DELETE correctly no-ops against a row a newer session has already overwritten, under either write ordering.

trigger: cache staleness applies to identity attributes (hostname/os/arch/agent_version), not just liveness
summary: PresenceIdentity fields can be up to 3s stale when matched against scope predicates — within the documented eventual-consistency tolerance but not explicitly called out as its own staleness dimension.
disposition_note: Accepted as within tolerance; not separately documented this round.

trigger: cache-stampede concern under a concurrent-caller burst
summary: Verified: presence_cache_mu_ correctly serializes concurrent live_presence() callers into one Postgres query per TTL window (a blocked caller re-checks the timestamp after acquiring the lock). Real cost is synchronous blocking under a large burst, not a correctness bug.
disposition_note: No action needed — informational, correctness verified, finding does not hold as a defect.

trigger: a Postgres blip during query_live_ids caches an empty result for the full 3s TTL

disposition_note: Accepted trade-off: bounded (3s), observable (sre-1's counter), and consistent with the cache's documented staleness tolerance. No fix applied this round.

trigger: migration v3's last_seen_at column uses DEFAULT now(), a VOLATILE default that does not qualify for Postgres's fast (PG11+) metadata-only ADD COLUMN path the way v2's constant-default columns did
summary: The migration-ladder doc's 'additive' description, read next to v2's genuinely-free additive columns on the same row, could mislead an operator into assuming this is also a zero-cost metadata-only change; it actually rewrites the table under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on every upgrade, every deployment (bounded in practice — row count = fleet size).
disposition_note: Fixed: row 58 updated with an explicit volatile-default rewrite note.

trigger: metrics.md's new table entry doesn't itself restate the slice's inertness on single-replica deployments

disposition_note: Not fixed — judged genuinely NICE-only; the surrounding section prose already makes clear this is HA-workstream groundwork, and metrics.md is not the primary place readers would look for deployment-topology framing.

trigger: a replica currently holding zero local agent sessions receives a dispatch request
summary: command_routes.cpp and forward_legacy_command both short-circuit on AgentRegistry::has_any() (LOCAL-ONLY, unmodified by this slice) BEFORE presence is ever consulted — a healthy presence-visible fleet is rejected with a false 503 'no agent connected'. Deterministic, not a race.
disposition_note: Fixed: new AgentRegistry::has_any_reachable() (checks live_presence() when has_any() is false) replaces has_any() at both call sites (command_routes.cpp:538, server.cpp's forward_legacy_command). Test added: 'has_any_reachable() checks presence, unlike has_any()'.

trigger: an agent reconnects to the SAME replica under a new session before the old session's disconnect handler runs (ordinary Wi-Fi-blip churn)
summary: remove_agent_if_session returned void and both disconnect handlers fired the durable OfflineEndpointStore::remove_if_session delete unconditionally, regardless of whether the LOCAL removal matched. Since the durable row's session_id is heartbeat-driven (not registration-driven), the stale session's disconnect notice can still match and delete a LIVE agent's presence row.
disposition_note: Fixed: remove_agent_if_session now returns bool (true iff it removed the CURRENT session); both call sites (agent_service_impl.cpp, gateway_service_impl.cpp) gate the durable delete on that return value. Test added: 'remove_agent_if_session reports whether it removed the CURRENT session'.

trigger: forward_legacy_command's Broadcast dispatch has a degraded gateway-directory read for at least one candidate

disposition_note: Fixed: added the missing 'else if (result.route_unreadable)' branch to the sent==0 cascade, mirroring command_routes.cpp's identical branch; corrected the stale comment.

trigger: OfflineEndpointStore::upsert (the sole writer of cross-replica liveness) degrades on every heartbeat
summary: Only the read/delete paths called record_presence_store_failure; a saturated/failing writer would age out presence fleet-wide with the counter reading zero throughout.
disposition_note: Fixed: upsert()'s two failure branches now call record_presence_store_failure(metrics_, "upsert", ...). Docs updated (metrics.md, observability-conventions.md).

trigger: reading docs/postgres-migration-ladder.md's v3 row as a correctness claim about DEFAULT now()'s volatility
summary: A prior fix (this same PR, governance Gate 6 enterprise-readiness round) claimed DEFAULT now() is VOLATILE and forces an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE table rewrite — factually WRONG. now() is STABLE (pg_proc.provolatile='s'), evaluated once at ALTER TABLE time, and qualifies for Postgres's fast metadata-only ADD COLUMN path. Empirically re-verified independently (relfilenode unchanged before/after against a live Postgres 18) before accepting this correction.
disposition_note: Fixed: row 58 corrected. Supersedes the earlier (wrong) g6-er-1 disposition note's underlying CLAIM, though g6-er-1 itself (the original missing-doc-note finding) is not retroactively edited — this is a NEW finding about a NEW defect the fix for g6-er-1 introduced.

disposition_note: Fixed: renamed governance.d/ha-ws5-shared-presence.v2Ttln.jsonl -> governance.d/4745-ha-ws5-shared-presence.v2Ttln.jsonl, run_id updated in every row to match.
